diffs.diff: pin count: part has 11 (A1 A2 A3 A4 A5 A6 A7 A8 A9 A10 GND), datasheet reading has 20 (A1 A2 A3 A4 A5 A6 A7 A8 A9 A10 C1 C2 C3 C4 C5 C6 C7 C8 C9 C10)
diffs.evidence: Both readings agree on the bare DC10EWA: the Kingbright datasheet (page 1 schematic) shows ten independent LEDs, anodes on pins 1-10 (side with the 'Anode mark' at pin 1) and cathodes on pins 20,19,...,11 (segment n = anode pin n, cathode pin 21-n). The second reading lists those 20 raw pins (A1-A10, C1-C10). The model, as its description states, is an assembly: the DC10EWA plus a Bourns 4611X-101-331LF 11-pin bussed network, whose datasheet says the 101 circuit has resistors 'connected between a common bus (pin 1) and a separate pin'. Network pins 2-11 sit on cathode pins 20-11, so the ten cathodes C1-C10 are internal to the assembly and only the common bus (GND) is exposed: 10 anodes + GND = 11 nets. The 9-net difference is the deliberate inclusion of the resistor network, not a pinout error; anode numbering A1-A10 matches the datasheet exactly.
